newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea accuses South ships of intrusion.
newsitem.headline: North Korea accuses South ships of intrusion.

text.p: Pyongyang on Friday gave its version of a clash between North and South Korean naval vessels, saying Seoul was to blame for the incident.

"On 5th June, the South Korean puppets committed a grave armed provocation by illegally infiltrating warships deep into our waters in the West Sea (Yellow Sea) and firing guns at our peaceful fishing boats," North Korean Radio said in a broadcast monitored in Tokyo.

On Thursday, the South Korean Defence Ministry reported that North and South Korean naval vessels exchanged fire after a Northern patrol boat strayed into South Korean waters with a fleet of nine fishing boats.
The ministry said the North Korean boat fired three rounds at three South Korean naval ships as they steamed to intercept, and that the Southern side returned fire with two rounds.

There was no damage, the Seoul statement said, adding that the North Korean boats sailed back across the nautical demarcation line after a 40-minute confrontation off the west coast of the Korean peninsula.
The demarcation line that bisects the Korean peninsula and extends into coastal waters is a legacy of the 1950-53 Korean War, which ended in a truce.
Friday's North Korean radio report said South Korean warships tried to seize North Korean fishing boats.

"In a bid to kidnap our peaceful fishing boats, at around 1333 (0433 gmt) three warships of the puppet army suddenly illegally infiltrated deep into our waters south of Kangnyong County...and rushed towards our fishing boats to surround them," the radio said.

"When a naval patrol ship of the (North) Korean People's Army...made an emergency entrance onto the scene, the rascals, unable to achieve their insidious goal, hurriedly fled southward after brutally firing at our fishing boats," it said.
It said the "provocation" did not develop into an armed clash because the North Korean soldiers displayed "great patience and self-control".
